product_name: Apple HomePod (2023, 2nd Generation)
headline: Okay for movies/TV - awful for bass rich music
review_text: These speakers are okay for the casual listener and someone who is using them primarily as a television or movie sound. The processing does some unusual manipulation with the high end and completely mangles the low end. Worse these the consumer Bose products do. For 600 (pair) you can get a much more powerful home theater system and/or significantly cleaner reference speakers that will be more accurate and more powerful. Siri still hasn't matured to what I'd call usable yet. How long has that product been available? It's pretty astonishing. At lower volumes and with content that isn't bass rich they sound spacious and open. There is a bit of "slipperiness," I don't care for on the top end but it doesn't make them unusable. These have internal transformers for power so you're only going to have two regular plugs instead of another pair of wall warts pushing aa USB cord. The sound everywhere feature is nice but can be done for a heck of a lot less money while winning even more functionality. There is no audible room measuring process. I'm not sure it does anything or not but their site suggests it "knows," where it is in a room. There is no EQ or user adjustable settings someone with more experience or more particular preferences would want. The low end is flabby and undefined on EDM and trance. Does well with Classical and movies. There is a "reduce bass," option but it seemed to completely eliminate the low end. Getting to these and/or other home pod speakers is clunky and terribly unintuitive. Sumarizing I think you can get better speakers with more power and more features for a heck of lot less money. I am trapped in an all apple home infrastructure and they aren't up to par for price or function for me. I produce and engineer music and favor reference monitors. For this price you can get an entry level setup with a subwoofer. For around 300 you can get a pair of JBL305p. For another 400 you can get the 10" sub. If you want room correction IK Multidmedia sells the iLoud MTM as a pair with the mic for aoround 800. The Apple "it just works," doesn't anymore. It took some time to update the firmware and wasn't very informative while it was doing so. Way more expensive than they should be for what they are. If you have a picky ear and/or want features or access to features this isn't the product for you. If you're okay with the inflated price, the terrible user experience, and the flabby low end for EDM or if you're using it for TV or movies they're okay. For my money there are plenty of options that do what this product does for a fraction of the price. The small ones, for what they are, are pretty impressive. These didn't wow me like I wanted them to.

Openinging my camera views on my Wyze camera takes a long time. Also, why does google have to make their AC plug so big? It covers up another socket. I like the features of the hub and as a clock and music player it works well as the sound quality has enough mids and bass for adequate sound quality but lacks hardware support to function smoothly. Does not support Amazon music as a native app but it has Spotify, strange. I also wish when I get notifications on my phone for my front door camera it would also show up on the Nest Hub. review_text: I bought this as an alarm because of the "gentle wake"features and wanting to move my phone away from my bed so it's not the first thing I use in the day... I assumed that "gentle wake" would include an alarm volume that slowly ramps up, but it doesn't. What you can have is birds chirping before your alarm blasts you out of bed and wake the whole family up.I'm not sure who is a light enough sleeper to have birds wake them up, but it's not me. I'm pretty disappointed overall. I've now gone back to using my phone, so I guess this was a waste of money for me.

headline: Disappointingly unreliable
review_text: Alarms disappear when stopped so I cannot use the Nest Hub as a bedside clock. I cannot just choose a specific podcast episode from my subscriptions, just a curated list of podcasts some of which I'm not subscribed to. It frequently looses WIFI signal even though the smart plugs and other devices in the room stay connected. The sound is nice. The screen is good and I like the picture frame aspect Nest video doorbell integration is good.

product_name: Google Nest Hub (2nd Gen) Smart Display
headline: Missing basic functionality
review_text: Does what it does well, but that's not much. It can show webpages, but you can't actually open a browser and navigate to one. It will walk you through a recipe, but only from approved providers. Google assistant works well and it will let you manage some of your home control, but not any features that haven't been added to Google Home nor will it show you what's currently playing on your non-Google smart home speakers or TV (i.e. Sonos). You can play your recommendations from Spotify and Youtube but can't search with text or use the actual apps for those services nor can you play to your Roku or Sonos. Just a simple cheap screen that lets you do whatever you've already setup through Google Home and nothing more. If I could just send any old webpage from my phone to this screen it would have a third start at least.

product_name: Google Nest Hub (2nd Gen) Smart Display
headline: Not impressed
review_text: I can't think of anything good about this display. The display is underwhelming with washed-up colors and no way to adjust the display settings. Everything needs to be done via voice or from a smartphone. Almost no controls are available on the display. Casting from an Android phone stops randomly. The clock faces are very limited and ugly. Why there is no clock face on a pure black background? No way to turn off the device unless you unplug it. An on/off button would make sense to me. Should I keep going? No, I think I'll stop here.

headline: Randomly Wakes Me Up In the Middle of the Night
review_text: This is marketed as a sleep monitor/sensor to help improve your sleep.It fails spectacularly at that.It succeeds amazingly in one thing: Making you sleep worse.It has a sunrise alarm (theoretically) that is supposed to be able to wake you with just light. Everyone else that does this understands that it should start out with minimal brightness and very red and slowly transition to brighter and bluer. This starts out at maximum brightness immediately. Furthermore you CANNOT turn off the noise alarm (or delay the noise alarm) so that you are actually woken up by the light. This makes the sunrise alarm worse than useless.The display will randomly make noises or turn the screen on for a second or two during the night. So it WILL wake you up with light.. even if you didn't set an alarm... but not at the correct time.The settings for this are distributed among at least 5 different apps it's nearly impossible to configure. It can't self-configure.The output "suggestions" are garbage

Trying to set up and use routines was also finicky and complicated, aggravated by how slow the hub is to respond in general. Took ages to set up a simple routine of turning on the lights in the bedroom when telling google good morning - and even then it took so long for the routine to run I might as well have gotten up and manually flicked a switch.

headline: Great but delicate
review_text: The Google Nest Hub is amazing. You can watch a picture frame of your favorite photos, listen to music, watch Netflix and listen to the news. This is made worse by the delicate condition of the device. A drop on the floor can cause the hub to chip and the screen to crack. This wouldn't be so bad if there were a protective case to buy, but as far as I could tell, there isn't one available anywhere. So, if you buy the Nest Hub, be very, very careful with it.

review_text: The hub is nice, responds well to commands but connections are a royal pain in the behind. My complaint is more about the Google Home app than the actual hub. GE smart bulbs are touted as the best for Google Home but I have yet to have one actually connect like they should. product_name: Google Nest Hub (2nd Gen) Smart Display
headline: Hit and miss
review_text: I got one of these for free from the Google One 2TB deal and decided to get another. If I'd known functionality would be relatively crippled compared to Alexa I may have been less inclined: there is no motion sensing support or other such triggers which really give your house that space-age feeling. Besides that, on rare occasions devices will disconnect randomly despite getting a strong 5g signal from a nearby repeater, and the voice interpretation is sometimes completely wrong even after weeks of training itself with my voice samples. Once I was speaking directly into my kitchen hub and my workspace hub 50 feet away responded.All of these are software issues and I feel the hardware is a good deal for the price, so the question is how much do you trust Google to follow through with updates? If you're embedded into the Google ecosystem as I am you probably don't have a lot of choice, but know that Google's Smart Home system still seems to be in "early-adopter" phase.

It is a tablet that should at least allow me to perform the simple task of opening up the streaming apps and browsing through their selections. review_text: This is definitely the most basic smart home touchscreen I can imagine a company like Google selling. It gets by, but barely. Video quality is acceptable, though it would be moreso as a secondary viewer (perhaps in a foyer niche or other restrictively small area). Touch controls aren't zippy, but faster than downright sluggish. Everything is slightly below middle ground compared to their more premium Hub Max. If you're looking for good quality YouTube videos and sound for the kitchen or an eye-catching display, this isn't the one. For a basic, no frills utilitarian purpose, I would recommend buying it on sale.

product_name: Lenovo Smart Clock Gen 2 - Blue
headline: A pretty solition with pretty stupid problems.
review_text: I love the aesthetic and the way the wireless charging base used magnets and pogo pins to attach to the clock. The speckled plastic on the wireless charging base compliments the fabric of the clock nicely. The Google Assistant is as responsive and intelligent as ever but it's responses and anything else you may want to play from this device are hampered by subpar speakers. They lack clarity and dont quite get loud enough to hear a query response from across the room. Google also hasn't figured out a way to separate which of its devices will answer the call of OK Google. On Amazon Alexa based devices, only the device closest to you will wake up and start listening for commands but it seems with Google Assistant devices, all nearby assistant enabled devices including smartphones will actuvate and listen theough the entire query. The command will only be started on one device, but ghe interruption is needlessly jarring. If, for example, you are listening to music on your phone while writing a document on your Chromebook and then to ask the Lenovo clock to turn the lights off, the clock will listen but the Chromebook will also pull up the assistant and stop responding to keyboard input, and the phone will pause the music while it listens for commands and will not automatically resume playback even when the clock turns the lights off. The built-in LED night light also has no manual controls. It seems to turn on for an indeterminate amount of time when it senses the room lights turn off but will often turn itself on in the middle of the night if it detects a minor fluctuation in room brightness. I ended up turning it off. All together and elegant package from Lenovo hindered by Google's lackluster software implementation.

product_name: Lenovo Smart Clock Gen 2 - Blue
headline: Good Bedside Clock with Charger
review_text:
The Lenovo Smart Clock 2 is an update from a previous model and includes a charging dock for your smartphone.

It features a 4-inch display that would be hard to read from a distance unless you would place it on your bedside as an alarm.

This update looks quite similar to the previous model. Lenovo has improved it by raising the display slightly and placed the speakers in the front. Software operates almost exactly like the original Smart Clock. Why offer a newer model with the same software?

This clock uses Google Assistant so you can play music, ask questions just by saying "OK Google." It uses YouTube music as well.

The Smart Clock 2 operates very similarly to the original Smart Clock. The installation instructions come up on your display when you set it up. It tells you to go to the Google Home app and follow its instructions.

One of my main negatives is that the Smart Clock does not come with any detailed instructions. Forget going to the Lenovo website for more help in setting it up as it is hard to reach technical support.

One of the nice features of this Smart Clock is that it comes with a charging pad on which to place the clock and your smartphone for charging. In addition, there is a port on the back that lets you plug in an additional device such as a smartwatch.

The Lenovo Smart Clock 2 works as advertised with basic functionality. If you want more help from Lenovo, good luck!

product_name: Lenovo Smart Clock Gen 2 - Blue
headline: Not that smart if you use Apple Music
review_text:
The Lenovo Smart Clock 2 fell short of my expectations for a few key reasons, but lets first look at some positives.
1. The charging dock worked great. I was able to charge my iPhone and AirPods without any issue, and even the battery case I use with my phone. For this reason, at least for now this clock will have a place on my nightstand.
2. The clock itself has some neat display options, including Google Photos and some fun presets. I've included photos of my favorite setting which using words instead of numbers and is a fun, unique display I've not seen before.
If we stopped here, and only bought the clock for the clock display options, and dock feature, I'd happily recommend the product. Unfortunately, the smart clock is also designed to be smart, and thats where it falls short. To be fair, I don't know if the failure is with the clock or with Google Home integration. Overall, if your primarily looking a great wireless charging dock with a built in nightlight and alarm clock attached, this is a good buy. Otherwise, I'd probably suggest a true smart display with a separate dock.

product_name: Lenovo Smart Clock Gen 2 - Blue
headline: REALLY Wanted To Like This, But 3.5 Stars As Is.
review_text:
I have had the same clock radio/alarm next to my bed for years and I was really looking forward to the Lenovo - Smart Clock 2 bringing my nightstand into the 21st Century. But as it stands right now, I think I'm going back to my old clock radio.
As a device, Lenovo build a nice, compact, and highly functional piece of electronics (even if their choice of plastics stinks). There is absolutely ZERO wrong with the form and function of the Smart Clock 2. Software-wise, I'm not sure what is Lenovo and what is Google. Either way, I think the core functionality is a tad too limited.

If you are deeply rooted in the Google universe and have an Android phone, you will get the most out of this Smart Clock. If you have an iPhone and are in the Apple ecosphere, you will not. If you value privacy, this is just a fancy charging base, if you are willy-nilly with your information, this thing can do a ton for you.

It's small, portable, and does just enough assisting with small daily tasks, such as an alarm, "Hey, Google", weather, music, etc. It doesn't have all of the functionality that a bigger unit/monitor would have but it performs great for those smaller more important tasks.

There are a few things I've noticed, which I'm sure are just software updates. I've found several times throughout the day, also in a span of a few days, I would notice the unit restart itself. It is always random. It doesn't change my settings but it will just cut off and then back on with its logo and then on again as if nothing happened.

product_name: TCL 32" Class 3-Series HD 720p LED Smart Roku TV - 32S355
headline: Great Smart TV for Small Rooms
review_text: TCL put time and thought into this TV.  What I noticed with the TV and its packaging is that every part that is to be assembled by the customer is perfectly laid out. All you have to do is follow the instructions in the handy quick start insert in the box.  I put the TV together on my own with a Phillips.  TCL paid attention to the legs(stand) and made sure to provide silicone pads for the bottom so furniture is protected from buffing or scarring and the screws and grooves to assemble the legs came with a place holder so when screwing in the legs everything stays in place so no damage to the  threading occurs when attaching the legs.  The Input and Output panel at the back is easy to identify and connect cords.  The TCL 32" was delivered on time  as promised.  I would add an additional audio to this unit if I was to share this TV with a room or crowd and mount it for better viewing quality.  Overall I am satisfied with my purchase, price and it came quickly, in one piece and was a breeze to set up.  I would recommend this TV for a small room or area and have it mounted for better viewing quality.

product_name: Google - Nest Learning Smart Wifi Thermostat
headline: Nice looking, mediocre functionality
review_text: This thermostat looks nice, better than any other thermostat. The installation and general setup is OK, it takes about about 30 minutes if all wiring is there.  It also easily integrates with Samsung SmartThings v2. But the functionality is not as advanced as for instance Ecobee's. The occupancy sensor in Nest thermostat is pretty much useless. I was home moving around, and the Nest thermostat would switch to Away state thinking that there is noone home. The remote sensor that came with it does not have an occupancy detection, so all you can count on for occupancy detection is really the smartphones of the people that live in the house, which is not  a really nice way of detecting home occupancy. If you have multiple sensors in the house you only can pick one at the time to regulate on its measure temperature, there is no possibility of averaging in this thermostat. Also, the history view is really poor for Nest, Ecobee did a much better job on this. And if you download the history data from the website, the status data is in JSON format and it is impossible to interpret. Also, the deadbands are not adjustable for Nest, at least I could not  find it. I did not try its learning feature myself since it already had a lot of negative comments. So, I think if one wants to buy a nice stylish looking thermostat for a very basic use, Nest Learning Thermostat is a very good choice. But if one wants a highly customizable thermostat which one can also regularly monitor and adjust, then there are better choices , like Ecobee.

headline: Could be better with smaller heat/cool temp spread
review_text:
I do like Nest products, but this one kinda frustrates me. I bought the extra thermostat sensors (3 of them) and placed them around the house. I set the app up to prioritize the Living Room thermostat during the day and my 1 year old's room at night. My goal was to keep the important rooms around 69 degrees all day._x000D_
_x000D_
The closest setting I can use to accomplish this goal is Heat & Cool mode @ 67-70. Guess what... The dang thing kicks heat on at ~66.5 degrees and cool air at ~70.5 degrees. That is way cold and way warm in our house. To make matters worse, I gave it a moving target by changing the priority room once a day. Add in the 1-2 degrees that our son's sensor is off by and you get a useless set of electronics._x000D_
_x000D_
I simply wish to keep my son's room warm enough at night and the living room cool enough throughout the day. Ideally, I could say keep ALL rooms at 68-69 degrees ALL day, but these products don't let me._x000D_
_x000D_
So why 3 stars, because it's pretty awesome beyond that. I just wish I could set this thing up and never look at it again. Until they make the add on sensors more accurate, enable "keep all rooms above/below X degrees" and reduce the minimum temp spread in heat-cool mode to 1 degree, I will have to tinker with it 3 times a day, which isn't ideal.

review_text:

_x000D_
As far as the thermostat itself, the physical device has a great design and is easy to adjust. Turning the dial echoes back to old thermostats while being very readable. It’s the best design I’ve seen._x000D_
_x000D_
As for the “smart” part? My wife and I dislike it. Change the temperature once because you’re uncomfortable? Nest tries to make a rule of it. You like it 2 degrees warmer on Saturday afternoons now. Now you have to delete that rule on their terrible calendar screen in the app. It ends up making you never change the thing._x000D_
_x000D_
And it has power saving modes when you are not at home. Be careful to set it to something reasonable or prepare to be freezing cold when you get home following a winter holiday. The promise of smart thermostats is that you could turn the heat back on remotely before going home, but who remembers to do that?

Our thermostat is in an area that we never pass by so we never trip its sensor to let it know we are home.  We adjusted all of the setting to try to get it to stop switching to eco mode on its own, including turning off all triggers and sensors and even turning off Home/Away Assist which should stop it from automatically going into eco mode.  Nothing worked, it still would go into eco mode on its own after a few hours of manually changing the temp.  The only thing that stopped this was for use to connect our phones to nest and turn on location so the nest knows when we are home.  The only other option we did not try was a factory reset, but others have said this did not work for them.

Google voice is where my problems start and end. They don't seem to speak the same language from time to time. I'll have Google tell me it can't adjust my thermostat, because "it is in eco mode", as it's changing my thermostat. Which just tells me Google doesn't know what it's doing._x000D_
Then there is coming home to a very cold house because the preheating isn't working. Supposed to work off my location and after telling Google we are heading home, it's supposed to up the heat when we are about 15 minutes away. Nope. So I scheduled the stat to do it automatically. product_name: Google - Nest Learning Smart Wifi Thermostat
headline: I WISH I KNEW
review_text: I should have read more reviews. There are lots of things I like about this thermostat, although it comes up short; and I bought four for my home and am now committed! The biggest gap is that there is no HOLD TEMP feature. I had to turn off learning and delete schedules to use two of them like manual thermostats; a waste of money other than the ability to adjust from my phone. Next, I had a lot of set-up issues; multiple attempts per thermostat were required.  Finally, the AWAY feature or Geofencing has yet to work. This was very important to me. I really like the Remote Sensor functionality, although already had a problem. After running fine for several days, one sensor disconnected from its thermostat. After much troubleshooting, I found that the sensor was fine and I had to reset the connected thermostat. The learning feature is nice, but without the other features I mentioned, it’s just another thermostat. I feel I could have spent less and received equal or superior results with another brand, such as the Honeywell T9.

product_name: Google - Nest Learning Smart Wifi Thermostat
headline: Lasts if you set up properly.
review_text: Most important thing to consider- check your thermostat wiring to confirm how many wires you have (typically 4 or 5). If you do not have a 'common' 5th wire to constantly feed power, the battery will die and no longer take a charge after about 1 year. It claims it will, but not the case; MANY will confirm this. I even tried swapping the battery, but had the same issue of it dying and no longer turning on my furnace. If you have 5 wires, it will constantly feed the power it needs and you should be good. They even have special "add-a-wire" kits to easily convert it to a 5-wire system. I highly recommend you get a 5th wire ran before setting up. Other than this common problem, it's a great product.

headline: Terrible - RMAs every unit!
review_text:
Allow me to regale you with the saga of my ongoing tryst with the Google Nest—an experience that can only be described as a comedy of errors, though not the kind one willingly signs up for._x000D_
_x000D_
In the span of four months, I've exchanged pleasantries with the Google Nest team no fewer than four times through the RMA process. Alas, the recurring protagonist of this tale is an error code that appears to be as persistent as it is unyielding, steadfastly refusing to yield to my earnest attempts at resolution._x000D_
_x000D_
The primary function of any technological device, especially one graced with the Google moniker, is to seamlessly connect to WiFi. Regrettably, this Nest seems to have enrolled in the School of Selective Connectivity, demonstrating a penchant for obstinacy that rivals the most intransigent of algorithms. Troubleshooting has become an unwelcome pastime, eclipsing the actual utility of the device._x000D_
_x000D_
In my quest for a harmonious relationship between the Nest and my router, I have traversed the labyrinth of customer support, diligently following each prescribed step in vain. One might be forgiven for assuming that this device, in its sheer audacity, harbors a disdain for the very concept of a wireless connection._x000D_
_x000D_
In the realm of smart home technology, where reliability is paramount, this Google Nest has managed to distinguish itself—not for its prowess, but for its uncanny ability to elude the embrace of WiFi. It's as if the device has chosen a path of technological asceticism, abstaining from the digital communion it was designed to facilitate._x000D_
_x000D_
If only the Nest were as adept at fostering connections as it is at generating error codes, we might find ourselves in a state of technological bliss. Alas, the reality is one of perpetual frustration, prompting me to consider alternative means of communication—perhaps carrier pigeons or smoke signals would prove more dependable._x000D_
_x000D_
In conclusion, the Google Nest, with its error-ridden escapades, has earned a dubious position on the roster of ill-fated purchases. Here's to hoping that future iterations will be more inclined towards harmonious cohabitation with WiFi networks, sparing others the exasperation that has defined my own journey.

headline: Not a very “smart” thermostat
review_text:
I’ve had my Nest thermostat for over a year and was SHOCKED to find my energy costs going UP and increased maintenance required on my Lennox Furnace system._x000D_
_x000D_
I spent so much money on this system because I thought it was “smart,” but honestly it’s got some of the dumbest, unintuitive features and settings._x000D_
_x000D_
I started paying more attention to why my furnace was working so hard and found out it was short-cycling. Meaning that even though I have my furnace on a schedule, the heat clicks on throughout the day for about 1 minute, shuts off for 2-3 min, then turns BACK on for another min, and so on. (The schedule I have set is supposed to heat to 68 degrees at 9 am then drops to a set temperature of 62 degrees during the day, then heats back to 68 degrees at 6 pm and drops to a set temperature of 62 degrees overnight - sidenote: if you choose to set a temperature schedule through the nest, you can’t set a different temperature on the schedule within an hour of the initial set temperature, otherwise I would have my house heat to 68 at 9 am and then drop to 62 at 9:30 am, but no, the earliest I can set the next, lower temperature, is 10 am, a full hour after the house heats and has been maintaining the initial set temperature, so dumb!)_x000D_
_x000D_
After I realized my system was short-cycling due to the nest thermostat, I spent hours searching through convoluted “help” articles from Nest. This is how I found out that the thermostat is constantly trying to heat the house and keep it set to the TENTH OF A DEGREE. Meaning that if I set my thermostat to heat to 68 degrees, the thermostat will assign a temperature of 68.6 degrees Fahrenheit. After it heats to that temperature, anytime it drops down to 68.5 degrees Fahrenheit, the whole system clicks on and heats the house back up to 68.6 degrees. Ideally, you’d be able to set the “hysteresis” or a timer on the thermostat (especially on a $200+ thermostat equipment) so that the temperature could be set to something like 72 degrees, heat to that temperature, and then not switch back on to heat the house for a set period of time or until the temperature in the house drops to a certain temperature like 68 degrees._x000D_
_x000D_
This lack of intuitive settings on the Nest is costing me a FORTUNE between furnace maintenance and increased energy costs (kind of crazy when the Nest is supposed to be so “eco friendly”!) and I’m considering switching back to my $15 Honeywell thermostat which is insane. Until they add this feature to the Nest thermostat, I warn you to steer away from this equipment!

product_name: Google - Nest Learning Smart Wifi Thermostat
headline: Dubious Quality Control And Unreliable Support
review_text:
I bought this unit to upgrade from Gen 2 because it can both make use of the sensors and it has dual-band WiFi for a stronger signal. It was very easy to install, it looks great, and it’s very intuitive to use, either on the wall, with your phone, or via a voice assistant. I’ll ding it a little bit because the sensor schedule—that is, when the device can be told to use which sensor—can’t be customized. You have 4 pre-set blocks to choose from, and that’s it. _x000D_
_x000D_
But then the trouble started. First I got a dreaded W5 error, meaning it’s WiFi radio was no longer working. I contacted Google for a replacement, which arrived promptly… but it kept getting caught in a boot loop and I couldn’t set it up. A second replacement arrived and wouldn’t correctly read my (very straightforward!) wiring, despite the fact that the one with the W5 error still could. The third replacement had the same issue, at which point I was advised to spend $130 to have a technician inspect my system to verify it was in fact the thermostat that wasn’t working. So after 6 total hours on the phone with customer support and HVAC technicians, and 3 replacement thermostats, I finally got my fourth one: an ecobee. I had it on and functioning in 20 minutes. _x000D_
_x000D_
My experience is probably very far outside the norm. I most likely just had a run of bad luck; I know when I see reviews like this for something I have maybe already talked myself into, I think, “ah but that’s just one guy; he’s unlucky or he did something wrong; that won’t happen to me.” And it probably won’t! But given the sheer number of issues I encountered—from failing components to annoying limitations to inept and sometimes contradictory customer support (who, at the end of the day, are call-center employees and decidedly *not* HVAC technicians)—I’d urge you to strongly consider other smart thermostats. This one is just not worth the risk or the headaches.

headline: no smarts, just a schedule.
review_text:
In short this app nor the product is very smart. The rigid adherence to the schedule is the largest issue. If I've changed the house temp 5min ago, I don't still want the thermostat to move to the sleeping temp at the scheduled time. The result is I find myself fighting the schedule more often than not and in the inverse I wake up in the middle of the night hot & sweaty for those night I'd forgot to turn the heat down (e.g. after I'd adjusted it after a schedule change). I'm unsure why this smart thermostat doesn't have the feature to return to the schedule after 2-4 hours of me making an adjustment as my last smart thermostat had. Even if we suspect that is a feature covered by a patent surely Google could use that big data it has on me from my Pixel, or my other nest devices to realize I've gone to sleep and that the regular scheduled program can be resumed._x000D_
_x000D_
Lastly, as many have pointed out here on other comments/posts, the Assistant needs to be able to exit ECO mode in one step. Why should I have to provide the two steps as if I'm performing some unsafe action by removing my house from ECO. The Assistant could simply chime back, "Okay, we've turned ECO off and set the temperature to 66 Degrees"._x000D_

product_name: Google - Nest Learning Smart Wifi Thermostat
headline: If you understand HVAC systems, buy it.
review_text:
TLDR: If you know how low voltage systems work, buy it. If you are not comfortable with HVAC troubleshooting, this may not be for you. _x000D_
_x000D_
Yes this thermostat is great to use. However, the setup could be difficult for so many folks that don't have an understanding of low voltage systems, and even for some DIYers. I started using it with 2 wire oil fired boiler to know how many hours my boiler runs. It is perfect for that. I used it just as a 2-wire thermostat with Rh and W. I have an understanding of how things work and I easily set it up with no issues. However, just like any other 2-wire thermostat without battery, you need to keep boiler switch on in order to have power through it when using 2 wires only. Many reviewers don't know why their nest learning thermostat doesn't work and rate it low and it's sad to see that. Even HVAC techs visiting my house warn me to not use nest and I always show them how easy it runs._x000D_
_x000D_
I recently switched to a gas 2-wire 24V system and installed another 24V transformer for Google doorbell and other LV systems for my house and now I run it with the boiler off in the summer. Why do I run it in summer? Because I have Google temperature sensors all over the house and it gives me relatively humidity reading near the thermostat and temps in the house so I can run window ACs where needed._x000D_
_x000D_
When running on 2-wire system, it did hum, but barely audible beyond a feet. Installing 24V external transformer with C/Rc wire combination resolved that (see photo - please excuse wire colors). There aren't many videos on how to do that, but you can do it. No wonder HVAC techs don't recommend it because it is so versatile and easy to troubleshoot. Don't rely on Google support because they don't know anything. Trust someone with knowledge in low voltage systems and you will be fine._x000D_
_x000D_
Other functions in the thermostat are cherry on top and I am waiting to use another one on a split system in future. I don't care about nest/home app being separate._x000D_
_x000D_
Are there any competitive thermostats at lower price? May be. Cheaper ones may not have relative humidity and analytics. Honeywell is comparable, but it's just a rectangle and Google learning thermostat does look good on a wall with its round shape. The touch and ring are smooth as well.
